events.title: Hill leaders brace for miserable 2027
events.summary: Have some sympathy for Capitol Hill's leaders next year, no matter who wins in November. 😩 Why it matters: The next Congress promises a thousand different ways to be miserable. And three of the big four leaders are expected to receive a two-year contract extension, with guaranteed long nights, bad days and short tempers. The fate of the fourth — Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) — rests on the outcome of the election. 🤕 The best (and worst) news for Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) is that the job as party leader is likely his if he wants it, even if Republicans lose the majority. Like his first two years as leader, Thune's next two will be marked by constant second-guessing , or worse, from a president who commands his party, crushes his opponents and questions Thune's courage . Then there's the GOP base. MAGA influencers are seething over Thune's reluctance to try to nuke the filibuster and jam through a voter-ID bill . Between the lines: Four of Thune's confidants — DHS Secretary (and former senator) Markwayne Mullin and Sens. Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and John Cornyn (R-Texas) — have left or are leaving the building. A fresh class of House conservatives will arrive in the Senate. They're likely to want to move fast and break things. The intrigue: Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) has not announced a third attempt to lead his party, but plenty of Republicans on the Hill suspect he will. Scott notably backtracked on his support for Thune in September. But Thune doesn't have to worry about his number two. Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) — who would be the top contender if Thune stepped down — has doubled down on his support. ⚠️ Thune's relationship with Speaker Johnson has been rocky throughout the year . If Republicans lose the House majority, Thune could find himself coordinating and strategizing with a new House leader. Most of Johnson's colleagues don't expect him to stay if the House flips. However, in the campaign's final weeks, Johnson has been playing Hamlet , publicly entertaining his next moves. With or without Johnson on stage, Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) and Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) are widely viewed as top contenders. 😎 Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) appears secure in his job as Democratic leader. His longevity in the role — or the Senate — is not. He's up for reelection in 2028 and could face a primary challenge from Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.). Many Democrats expect him to retire. One possible result: YOLO Chuck , a 76-year-old majority leader with an angry base and ambitious colleagues, but nothing to lose. 🤬 One urgent task for Schumer is to get on the same page as House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), whose progressive members have some strong feelings about Schumer and the Senate. Jeffries and Schumer took dramatically different approaches to funding the government in March 2025. These differences would be harder to manage in the majority, especially if Jeffries struggles to maintain discipline within his ranks. However, Jeffries — like Schumer and Thune — doesn't appear to have any formidable challengers for party leader. Jeffries could face many of the same headaches Johnson did — a wing of his party that ran on anti-establishment principles and whose votes cannot be counted on . What we're watching: Trump and Schumer have a complicated relationship . But the president has indicated he sees Jeffries as someone he could work with.

events.title: Porsche’s electric Macan Turbo is an automotive existential crisis
events.summary: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Maybe it was the grey color, the slightly bulbous roofline, or the vaguely SUV-like proportions of the electric Porsche Macan, but as I shuttled kids and groceries around city and suburban streets, I never once noticed a longing stare from other drivers. Unlike with other cars I’ve tested, no enthusiasts stopped to ask me questions. The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo simply blended in, leaving in its wake a raft of existential questions. What is a sports car, anyway? Does it need to be overwhelmingly extroverted? Should it match the leaner, lighter look of its gas-powered sibling? Drive one and the questions cease. Maybe that’s because the acceleration makes it hard to breathe? Or maybe it’s because, by the numbers, the Macan is a sports car at heart despite its rather humdrum crossover body style. My passengers would agree. The kids I drove to soccer practice, both my own and others, gave the punchy acceleration high marks. The G-forces it reports on the head-up display ($2,660) can easily mimic the pull of gravity. Stab the accelerator at 70 mph and it lurches as though it were standing still. (Don’t worry, fellow parents. I did not try that with children on board.) On winding roads, the car comes alive, thanks in part to the four-wheel steering ($2,150). Drop it into Sport Plus mode, and the car literally drops on its air suspension. Are we sure this is another anonymous crossover? Maybe anonymity is a useful trait in a car this responsive and powerful. Unlike most two-row crossovers, you get the feeling of sitting in the Macan, not on it. The wheel extends far enough to make a sporty driving position possible, and the classic Porsche chronometer ($1,040) perched atop the dash ticks off the seconds it takes to get the kid to soccer practice. The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo EV is a two-row crossover with 630 horsepower and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery. The EV, which the automaker provided to me for a week, starts at $112,700. However, the one I drove rang up at $149,610, including destination fees. Yes, the options alone could buy a nicely equipped Chevy Bolt . With Porsche and options, if you have to ask…well, it’s better not to. The Porsche Macan Turbo EV I drove came in Slate Grey Neo (a $2,620 upgrade), which was really well executed and among the best greys I’ve seen. If you crave luxurious anonymity, then this grey is your color. There were a slew of other options, and in my view, not all of them are worth it. I’d skip the passenger display ($1,710); my kids liked that it could play YouTube videos, but they can’t ride up front, and my wife was underwhelmed. “Our washing machine can play YouTube videos,” she said. I’d also forgo the illuminated Porsche wordmark on the front seatbacks ($690), puddle lamps that shine “PORSCHE” onto the pavement ($420), Porsche crests on the headrests ($640), and an illuminated Turbo badge on the door sills ($1,230). That Turbo badge became a point of contention for some of my friends, who were quick to point out that EVs technically can’t have turbos. That is true, though automotive names have long been divorced from reality. Almost every Porsche these days has a turbo, even those not labeled as such. It’s not just Porsche: BMW’s model numbers, for example, stopped reflecting engine displacement decades ago, and the Ford Galaxie never traveled between star systems using its hyperdrive. Sorry, friends, I’m not taking the bait. At least the Macan Turbo’s EV qualities don’t raise too many questions. It charges fast — exactly 20 minutes from 19% to 80% on a 350-kilowatt charger — and gets about 285 miles of highway range. Those big wheels ($4,110) and sticky tires ($660) sapped some range, but it was still more than enough to get from New York to Boston with charge to spare. The advanced driver assistance system ($1,140) works well enough, even if it hunts a bit in the lane. The AI-powered voice assistant did a solid job of interpreting my queries and commands. For a while, I thought it was the only way to turn on the heated steering wheel ($720), which was actually fine because it worked so well. (Surprise! There’s a small button hidden on the inner rim of the steering wheel between two spokes. IYKYK, I guess.) When it’s time to leave the Macan, you can just open the door and walk away. The Burmester sound system ($4,960) will keep bumpin’ until you lock the door, which is a helpful reminder. If you’re a Porsche traditionalist, you can also hit the vestigial power button to the left of the driver’s display. Good to have choices, I guess? At least Porsche doesn’t charge you for that. The navigation system, and specifically how it integrates with the EV, was underwhelming. When the car was at a 22% state of charge, I asked it to find the nearest fast charger. It directed me to two.

events.title: Mine owner convinced tiny town's lead poisoning concerns are unfounded
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts IPC hearing on Bowdens Silver Mine concludes as lead concerns raised Protest signs outside the second day of hearings. ( ABC Central West: Hamish Cole ) The Independent Planning Commission (IPC) held a three-day hearing into a proposed silver and lead mine near Mudgee this week. A minerals expert told the IPC the nearby Lue Public School should be moved if the project was approved. The IPC is expected to hand down a determination by December 9. The NSW Independent Planning Commission (IPC) has been told a public school should be moved if a proposed silver and lead mine is approved, amid fears it could poison children. The IPC heard three days of evidence this week in Mudgee as it reassessed a proposal to extract 30 million tonnes of silver, lead and zinc over 23 years near Lue. The project has divided the community, with advocates touting the economic benefits and others raising concerns about potential environmental and health impacts. Proponent Silver Mines Limited's managing director Jo Battershill implored the panel to approve the development. "The project would provide investment and economic diversification for the mid-western region," he said. A tractor protest was held in Mudgee on Wednesday in opposition to the proposed silver mine. ( ABC Central West: Hamish Cole ) Almost 100 people spoke at the hearing, with the majority opposed to the mine. Only a few who spoke in support were not employees. On Wednesday, a group of farmers rode tractors and utes from Lue into Mudgee as part of their protest action. Along with dozens of local residents, experts from around Australia also addressed the hearing. Dozens of local residents spoke in opposition to the Bowdens Silver Mine at the IPC's reassessment. ( ABC Central West: Hamish Cole ) Among them was University of Queensland professor and principal research fellow at the Sustainable Minerals Institute Barry Noller. He told the hearing he believed the project's potential for lead exposure posed an unacceptable risk to children at Lue Public School, located two kilometres from the mine site. "I recommend that the Lue school, being at the boundary of dust deposition of [the] Bowdens mining project, be moved," Professor Noller said. "The management plan would be underestimating the true quantity of deposited lead that is relevant in terms of assessing the risk to adults and particularly children." Jo Battershill appeared before the IPC on Wednesday as part of its reassessment of the mine. ( ABC Central West: Hamish Cole ) Mr Battershill told the IPC that while the concern was understandable, the project had undergone extensive independent review. "Predicted health risks from the project, including from lead, are very low and are not expected to result in adverse human health impacts," he said. "It has been carefully assessed, and multiple layers of monitoring and management would apply throughout the life of the project." Mudgee-based general practitioner Peter Bryant told the panel dust from the project would threaten residents across the district. "There are no levels of lead exposure which are known to be without risk of harm," Dr Bryant said. "I don't want to find myself frequently requesting blood tests for children who live in this area to check their lead levels. "I really hope not to be talking with parents about the high levels of lead that have been found in their child's blood and discussing the long-term implications this could have on their blood development and ongoing health." GP Peter Bryant also spoke at the public hearing, citing his concerns. ( ABC Central West: Hamish Cole ) As part of the proposal, Silver Mines Limited would use approximately 2,000 megalitres of water a year for processing and dust suppression. events.title: ICE shooting leads to rare Jeffries-Mamdani collaboration
events.summary: An October shooting by federal immigration officers in New York City has led to a head-turning show of unity from House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Why it matters: This unlikely collaboration between leaders of Democrats' competing establishment and progressive wings shows how opposing Trump-era immigration enforcement has become an area of party consensus. Democrats "are definitely unified across the spectrum re ICE," Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), the chair of the Queens Democratic Party and a close ally of Jeffries, told Axios. He added that "the Mayor has also reached out ... to me in regards to local issues and I believe Leader Jeffries is also indicating he wants to work with the NY Congressional delegation." Driving the news: Mamdani led a letter dated Oct. 16 with over 100 other Democratic elected officials in New York City, including every Democratic member of the city's congressional delegation, to parking lot and garage owners. "In solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and in our shared commitment to the City we love, we ask that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations," the letter reads. The officials argued that the shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in New York's Marble Hill neighborhood in early October was "not an isolated case," pointing to past instances in Queens and Manhattan . "Owners who refuse to take part in these federal civil immigration enforcement operations advance public safety by protecting their own staff and customers, as well as fellow New Yorkers beyond their lots and garages." Between the lines: Jeffries and Mamdani have walked a careful line as two of the most prominent national figures within their respective Democratic Party factions. Jeffries rankled the left, including some members of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, by waiting until 11 days before last year's election to endorse Mamdani for mayor. The two came into conflict this summer when Jeffries supported Democratic Reps. Dan Goldman and Adriano Espaillat while Mamdani campaigned hard for their primary challengers, though the Democratic leader notably downplayed the clash . Yes, but: The two have also had other notable moments of accord, such as when Mamdani opposed City Councilmember Chi Ossé 's ultimately aborted plan to try to primary Jeffries from the left. They also appeared together at a ribbon-cutting for a housing development in Brooklyn on Thursday. Zoom out: The letter's signers also include Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), who accused then-candidate Mamdani last year of making "references to global jihad," for which she later apologized . Goldman and Espaillat, who were ultimately unseated by their Mamdani-backed challengers, signed on as well. So did retiring Rep. Nydia Velázquez, who was burned by Mamdani endorsing Claire Valdez over her chosen successor, according to the New York Times . What we're hearing: "It's significant to see Mayor Mamdani lead a letter like this that includes both U.S. Senators and the full NYC Democratic House delegation (including the two he opposed in this spring's primaries)," a prominent Mamdani ally said in a text message to Axios. The person added: "It reflects both how universally hated ICE is by Democrats — and how much work the mayor has done to build bridges." The Mamdani ally spoke on the condition of anonymity to offer candid analysis of the delicate relationship between the mayor and the party establishment. The bottom line: Others argued that Democratic unity around opposing ICE was the overriding factor. One Democratic elected official from New York told Axios: "The fact that everyone signed on has more to do with the power of the issue than the power of the Mayor." A person in Jeffries' orbit similarly argued that immigration is simply "a unifying issue for Dems," but acknowledged that Mamdani "is consistently reaching out to the delegation to build ties and smooth things since the elections, which is smart."

events.title: Private lenders scramble to recover funds after Bathla collapse
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Major Bathla lender La Trobe sells $31.2m loan as private credit firms seek to recover funds Topic: Construction and Real Estate Industry Private credit lenders of Bathla Group are striking deals to recover debts following the property giant's collapse. ( ABC News: Berge Breiland ) La Trobe Financial has sold its senior loan facility, tied to a Bathla Group development, to investors through a fund managed by 360 Capital. The $31.2 million purchase would give 360 Capital greater influence over the Marsden Park project. Morningstar expects private credit fund growth to slow substantially. The fallout from the collapse of property developer Bathla Group continues to reverberate through Australia's private credit market, with lenders taking matters into their own hands to recover money tied up in the failed construction giant. In one of the latest deals, property investment and funds management group 360 Capital has revealed it acquired a senior loan facility for about $31.2 million through its private credit fund, funded by private investors and entities within the 360 Capital group. A senior loan facility is the first mortgage debt in a commercial investment and ranks highest in repayment priority. The ABC understands the debt was acquired from major private lender La Trobe Financial, relating to a Bathla development at 137 South Street, Marsden Park, in Sydney's north-west. An artist's impression of 137 South St, Marsden Park apartments, as listed on the Bathla website. ( Supplied: Bathla ) The Marsden Park project comprises 72 apartments and is nearing completion, according to two sources close to the construction. Half of the apartments have already been pre-sold under contracts worth $25.8 million (excluding GST), 360 Capital said in a statement. In August, La Trobe disclosed it had $38.1 million in loans to Bathla, comprising four residential loans and one development loan. The ABC understands through this deal, La Trobe has sold its development loan, recovering all outstanding principal, interest and late-payment charges and significantly reducing its exposure to the collapsed developer. Deal gives 360 Capital greater control 360 Capital's ASX-listed mortgage investment trust, the 360 Capital Mortgage REIT, already held an $8.9 million loan secured against the development, which ranked behind La Trobe Financial for repayment. The trust has invested a further $5.2 million in the deal. Construction work has stopped at sites and the company is down to skeleton staff. "The step was not taken lightly, but is very important to protect the value of the trust's subordinated position," the company said. The deal means entities associated with 360 Capital now control both the first and second mortgages over the development, giving them greater influence over how the project is completed and the debts recovered. Morningstar equity analyst Winky Tan said lenders holding first mortgages were in a much stronger position to recover their money, while mezzanine lenders further down the repayment queue risked losing most, if not all, of their investment. "When you're able to finish the project, you can sell it as a finished product, which will have a much higher valuation than a half-finished project," she said. New Victorian laws reveal auction reserves, so buyers stop wasting weekends Lifestyle benefits outweigh costs of apartment living for some downsizers Real estate agents urged to 'enhance responsibly' as AI use rises Outcry over council's 'extortionate' fee hike on short-stay homes Following the purchase, advisory firm Wexted was appointed as receiver, with a focus on speeding up the process of obtaining occupancy certificates and settling the 36 pre-sold apartments. 360 Capital executive chairman Tony Pitt said the group expected to recover the full amount owed to it under the loan. Ms Tan cautioned that the ultimate financial outcome for any lender would depend on whether the remaining apartments could be sold and at what price, particularly given the downturn in the property market. 'Perfect storm' unfolding in private credit sector Lenders including Centuria Bass and CVS Lane suspended withdrawals from some funds in August amid concerns about their exposure to Bathla. MA Financial, which says it has no exposure to Bathla, also introduced withdrawal limits on some of its funds amid concerns more investors could seek to pull out their money. Major private credit manager Metrics Credit Partners, which also says it has no exposure to Bathla, suspended withdrawals from some unlisted funds amid scrutiny of asset valuations.

events.title: The AI behind Formula One race-day decisions
events.summary: Sunday, May 3, 2026, Miami International Autodrome, Miami Joseph “Joey” McMillan has been watching the numbers, and the skies above. With the start of the Miami Grand Prix just a few moments away, the Lead Race Strategist for the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team sits at his console, perched on the pit wall above the start line, listening to multiple different intercom channels at the same time, checking the weather reports and thinking about the race ahead. The team’s drivers have performed well over the race weekend, both in practice and in qualifying. British driver George Russell is starting fifth on the grid but, ahead of him, Kimi Antonelli is in pole position. The Italian teenager has been the breakout star of the season so far and is aiming to win his third Grand Prix in a row. At 19, Antonelli would be the youngest driver ever to achieve that feat. Antonelli and Russell are just two of Mercedes’ vast F1 team, around 1,300-strong, mainly engineers dedicated to making their cars go faster. But McMillan isn’t an engineer. His job is not about squeezing an extra ounce of speed from the engine, but saving time by executing a plan of action on the track, analyzing the variables his drivers can’t see and can’t control. “The strategist is sort of the black sheep in the sense that we are not really focused on making the car [go] faster,” explains McMillan. “Our job is to try and navigate those two cars through the race weekend. And to do that, we’re often looking at a lot more than just our car. We’re focused on every car on the grid, what every team is doing.” Like all sports, F1 is obsessed with marginal gains and McMillan’s mission is to find an edge on rival teams, making decisions based on multiple streams of data and running multiple simulations. In a sport where a thousandth of a second can be the difference between winning and losing, every factor needs to be considered. “By far the most important thing we do is decide what tire compounds to use in the race and what laps to make pit stops on,” he says. “That combination is known as the strategy.” There are five types of tires to choose from during a race, all color coded for different conditions: three types of slicks for dry conditions (soft, medium and hard), and two treaded tires (intermediates for light showers and wet tires for heavy rain). “If we knew the degradation rate of each of those compounds, essentially how much slower they get each lap in milliseconds, strategy would be so easy.” But things are rarely easy in F1. As well as monitoring the pace of rival cars and trying to judge how the tarmac will affect the tires, the strategy team’s simulations also need to know the answer to the question dominating McMillan’s thoughts as he sits at his trackside console. Is it going to rain? And in Miami, a storm is coming. The race is taking place at the start of May, six weeks before Florida’s Atlantic hurricane season usually begins, but the bad weather is ahead of schedule. The threat of lightning strikes is so severe that the organizers have brought the start of the race forward by three hours. Rain briefly fell in the morning, and McMillan is being fed local weather radar data that suggests rain might fall again during the race. Will it be a passing shower? Or a deluge? A decision has to be made about which tires to start on: the faster slicks, the intermediates or the wet tires. That choice could win or lose the race before it even starts. McMillan and the team make a play based on the data at hand and their instincts. The drivers will not start on wet tires, they will be on slicks and hope the weather holds. As the lights go out and the race begins, the drivers roar toward the first corner on a dry track under skies pregnant with rain. And then all hell breaks loose. “When we run our simulations, we run an entire race. We want to run thousands, if not millions of these races. Now, with Azure Batch, we can” McMillan has been a race strategist for a decade. The softly spoken Englishman was hired by the Mercedes F1 Team after finishing his mathematics PhD at Imperial College London. It was his first job after college and he’s been there ever since, moving up to Senior Race Strategist and, eventually, Lead Race Strategist. “We use about five or six strategists a weekend,” he says. “Out of those, maybe one or two of them will ever end up being the pit wall strategist who’s making the final decision, but you need a whole lot of people running models.” Mathematics is only part of the job. What separates a good strategist from a great one is the ability to function under pressure. “It’s not super difficult in the sense that I don’t need high-level mathematics, nothing like the mathematics I was doing for my PhD,” says McMillan. “What makes a good general strategist? Someone who is a logical thinker, really good at modeling and data analysis. But what really makes you good at the pit job is to be able to make the decision in the moment, to do it very, very quickly, with very good communication skills… when you’ve got drivers, team principals, race engineers, lots of excitement and intensity. Once you realize you can do that, I think it’s pretty clear you’re going to be good at this.” Machine learning, as McMillan calls it, has always been a huge part of his job – but in recent years, AI technology has greatly improved his ability to analyze more and more data at faster speeds. “My day-to-day, the actual Sunday doing the strategy, hasn’t changed a huge amount yet,” he says. So, what has changed? “I write quite a lot of code, but I’m really not a coder. I’m a mathematician, a statistician, a game theorist, but I’m not a coder. I understand what data we’ve got. I understand what I’d like to do with it. And [with] the advent of AI, like coding tools, I can do those things a huge amount quicker. I can now write models, write analysis, do things at a speed I could never dream of before.” At the start of 2026, Microsoft signed a deal with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team, a partnership that put Microsoft technology at the heart of its operation. After dominating Formula One for much of the 2010s, winning seven consecutive drivers’ championships between 2014 and 2020 and eight consecutive constructors’ championships between 2014 and 2021, the team was looking to build on that legacy. With a radically reengineered car performing strongly in testing, there was growing belief that 2026 could see the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team challenge for championships once again. For the F1 strategy team, one of the biggest benefits of working with Microsoft is access to Azure’s vast cloud computing capacity. Using Azure Batch, they can run huge numbers of race simulations simultaneously, testing multiple scenarios before, and even during, a Grand Prix.

events.title: Celebrating the next generation of Latin American game creators
events.summary: Multiple Adventures Await as Stories: The Path of Destinies Arrives on Xbox One Upcoming Changes to XBOX Cloud Gaming Free Play Days – NBA 2K27, Crusader Kings III, The Alters, Bus Simulator 21, Soccer Story and Ravenswatch Coming to XBOX Game Pass: Battlefield 6, Valor Mortis, Forever Ago, and More Learn how XBOX is helping creators across Latin America bring new ideas to life through the ID@XBOX Developer Acceleration Program, the inaugural XBOX Game Camp Mexico City, and six upcoming titles from the region. Across Latin America, developers are creating some of gaming’s most distinctive new worlds by turning personal memories, local history, cultural traditions, and bold ideas into experiences that resonate far beyond the region. Games such as Despelote , Mexico, 1921: A Deep Slumber , and SOPA – Tale of the Stolen Potato show the remarkable breadth of this creative community, from intimate coming-of-age stories and interactive journeys through history to magical adventures filled with heart. For years, XBOX has worked alongside creators across Latin America, helping studios of all sizes bring their games to players around the world. Through the ID@XBOX Developer Acceleration Program (DAP), we’ve worked with more than 60 studios from Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Honduras, Uruguay, and beyond, helping developers bring over 30 culturally distinctive games to XBOX since 2023, while strengthening the region’s growing game development ecosystem by providing access to technical resources, business support, and mentorship. XBOX Game Camp Heads to Mexico City As XBOX continues to support game creators across Latin America, XBOX Game Camp is expanding its reach with a Mexico City debut on October 17 alongside Xbox FanFest. Taking place during Xbox’s 25th anniversary year, the event will celebrate Mexico’s game development community and the extraordinary talent already shaping games across the region, while creating new opportunities for developers to learn, connect, and grow. XBOX Game Camp Mexico will bring together a select group of Mexican studios, including developers both within and beyond the existing XBOX ecosystem, for a day focused on industry knowledge, community, and connection. The program will feature advanced developer seminars, keynotes and fireside conversations with industry leaders, along with opportunities to connect directly with industry professionals and members of Team XBOX, including Jens Bergensten, Chief Creative Officer at Mojang Studios. His fireside conversation with Peter Zetterberg, Founder of XBOX Game Camp, will explore his career journey and lessons from Sweden’s game development ecosystem, with a focus on collaboration, supporting fellow creators, and the role community can play in building a stronger industry. With a passionate development community and a strong culture of collaboration, Mexico City provides an ideal setting for XBOX Game Camp to celebrate locally developed games, strengthen connections across the ecosystem, and create new pathways for Mexican creators to bring their ideas to audiences around the world. As we support the next generation of creators through initiatives like XBOX Game Camp, we’re also celebrating the developers shaping Latin America’s game development community today. Here’s a look at six upcoming games from Latin American creators to keep on your radar. Six Upcoming Games from Latin America to Watch Mariachi Legends — Halberd Studios, Mexico Studio Contact: Miguel Hasson, Creative Director Studio location: Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico Mariachi Legends is a brutal, combat-oriented Metroidvania wrapped in gorgeous pixel art and set in the heart of Mexico. Players step into the shoes of Pablo Cruz, a Mexican detective who strikes a deal with Death herself. Granted the ability to transform into the supernatural entity “La Sombra,” Pablo must battle an evil syndicate known as the Mariachi Legends. It’s a journey that blends intense hack-and-slash action with RPG mechanics, all unfolding around the Day of the Dead festivities. What truly separates Mariachi Legends is our deep, authentic integration of Mexican culture and folklore directly into the gameplay loop. Beyond standard combat and exploration we’ve also introduced a unique culinary mechanic: players explore the world to collect ingredients and cook traditional Mexican dishes to gain strength. Coupled with a Day/Night cycle driven by Sun and Moon gates, where different map sections are accessible depending on the time of day, the game offers a distinct flavor you won’t find in other Metroidvanias. How has DAP supported development of your title? ID@XBOX has been instrumental in helping us bring our vision to life without compromising on quality or cultural authenticity. The program provided us with the resources and technical support needed to ensure Mariachi Legends runs flawlessly on XBOX Series X|S, utilize features like XBOX Play Anywhere. The marketing amplification and the opportunity to bring the game to a massive audience via XBOX Game Pass has given our studio the runway to focus fully on creating a polished experience. What do you hope players take away from your game? We hope players walk away with a profound appreciation for the richness of Mexican traditions. We want them to experience the thrill of a tight, challenging Metroidvania, but more importantly, we want the world, the food, the music, and the folklore of Mexico to resonate with them long after they put the controller down. Studio Location: Villa Alemana, Valparaíso, Chile In Colorbound , color is more than just a hue. Join Anku on a heartwarming journey, using color to shape the world around you. In this puzzle-platforming adventure, you will solve challenging puzzles, uncover secrets, and help a family of musicians reunite, just like in the old days, for a farewell concert. Colorbound stands out primarily for its aesthetics and core mechanics. The ability to change the colors of the environment creates an experience that draws attention through its very concept. Furthermore, the narrative, music, and art reflect the Andean culture of Latin America, successfully connecting with the region and showcasing a culture unknown to many. Primarily by providing some of the funding for the project’s production and post-production, which allowed for a faster development process and more comprehensive publishing work. On one hand, I hope that during the process you are surprised by the different mechanics associated with the colors and enjoy solving the game’s challenging puzzles. But above all, I hope you take away a fond memory of a simple, touching experience about friendship and grief. events.title: Trump: White House didn't impede satellite system in Ukraine
events.summary: President Trump said Friday that his administration did not disrupt an Elon Musk -owned satellite system used by Ukraine to wage war against Russia. Why it matters: The restrictions imposed earlier this week on the system hampered the Ukrainian military's ability to intercept Russian attack drones for 24 hours. It raised concerns that the Trump administration and possibly Musk were retaliating against Ukraine for its attacks on Russian oil refineries and President Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of Trump's diesel deal with Russia. What he is saying: "I just checked this morning — it wasn't us," Trump told reporters. "I don't know if it was anybody, because it wasn't me and I don't think it was Elon." He was responding to a question about a Reuters report that the order to slow the satellite system came from the White House. The other side: Ukrainian officials remain highly skeptical of Trump's claims and believe someone in the U.S. government participated in throttling the systems. "Our guys who speak to SpaceX say the White House was involved in the decision," a Ukrainian official said. Catch up quick: The Ukrainian military uses SpaceX's Starlink satellite communications system to control and operate its reconnaissance and intercept drones. When Starlink doesn't operate at full capacity, Ukraine's ability to gather intelligence, use interceptor drones and conduct long-range strikes against Russia is impeded. Ukraine relies on two satellite systems: One is SpaceX's Starlink, which it uses for communications, ground forces, logistics and defensive drones — ones that shoot down incoming drones. The other is Starshield, which is controlled by the U.S. government and used for offensive military purposes. Both systems were restricted, according to Ukraine. In a post on X on Wednesday, Musk hinted the U.S. government was involved in disrupting Starshield. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote. The big picture: The limitations came days after a new crisis erupted between the U.S. and Ukraine over Trump's agreement to lift sanctions on Russian oil sales. Zelensky criticized the move, then Trump called for Ukraine to elect a new president.

events.title: AOC and El-Sayed test-drive a national platform for the left
events.summary: The News ESCANABA, Mich. — Abdul El-Sayed and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez are already thinking beyond 2026, even though he’s not a senator yet. During three different stops Thursday on his Senate campaign’s bus tour through redder, rural areas of this swing state, El-Sayed and Ocasio-Cortez drew crowds that showed notable star power. While Republicans see Michigan as their strongest chance to pick up a Senate seat, the progressive pair are casting themselves as heirs to the broader movement that Bernie Sanders has commanded for a decade — a push they plan to expand beyond this state. “Once you elect one person like that, people will then catch on,” Ocasio-Cortez declared of El-Sayed in this paper-producing town, whose county last went Democratic in 2008. “And we will start electing more people like that.” In a region walloped by the sort of deindustrialization that President Donald Trump had returned to office pledging to reverse, El-Sayed drew loud applause for vowing to move beyond him: “Donald Trump is just the worst symptom of the disease of our politics — the disease of the system of allowing billionaires, corporations, special interest, the bought and sold politicians, the way that the money brings the system against us.” While Ocasio-Cortez has yet to make her decision on a 2028 presidential primary that she’d enter as an automatic contender, her Michigan tour amounted to calling her shot. She’s betting on El-Sayed as proof of concept for her brand of populism, embracing his play for the left in a tight Senate race even as the strategy sparks internal Democratic worries about a possible drift of Black and Jewish voters towards Republicans. If he defeats GOP nominee Mike Rogers in a remarkably anti-Trump cycle to become the first Muslim senator in US history, El-Sayed could spark his own presidential boomlet. But for the moment, in a state that’s now among the Democratic nominating calendar’s earliest to vote, his campaign served as a vehicle for Ocasio-Cortez to spell out more ambitious policy than a single candidate’s platform. When one attendee in Escanaba asked the duo about eliminating interest on student loans. El-Sayed said “you shouldn’t have to go into debt to get a higher education” and that Democrats should find creative ways around the Supreme Court’s rejection of a Biden-era student loan forgiveness program. Then Ocasio-Cortez went a step further, saying that student loans should be interest-free, public colleges should be tuition-free, and “we have to really be asking ourselves what is the utility of putting people in indentured servitude their entire lives for seeking an education.” The crowd cheered. (At another point, the New Yorker laughed off cries from supporters asking her to run for president.) Know More Although Democrats have often fallen short in this part of Michigan come November, it’s been favorable territory for progressives during primaries. In this year’s Senate primary, El-Sayed carried the three counties where he held events Thursday, as did Sanders during the Vermont independent’s 2016 Democratic presidential bid. “I just want to have a conversation about gas, groceries, the ability to see a doctor. Want money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for all?” El-Sayed told reporters. “I think that’s what Yoopers want, too.” He knocked Rogers, who generally avoids the large gatherings favored by the El-Sayed campaign, for not appearing in the Upper Peninsula this fall. “So when’s the last time he was in Iron Mountain? When’s the last time he was in Escanaba? When’s the last time he was in Marquette? I don’t know. At least I show up,” said El-Sayed. A Rogers spokesperson pointed to previous stops by his campaign in the Upper Peninsula towns over the last year, including in Marquette in June. “AOC is the latest trick up the Democrats’ sleeve, but Michiganders know better than to fall for it,” said the Rogers spokesperson. “While Abdul El-Sayed tries to run from his own progressive policies, AOC’s visit reminds voters exactly who he is — a radical leftist who wants to defund the police, force EV mandates on Michiganders, and jack up our utility prices even higher.” Rogers is keeping the race close in most polls, while undeniably benefiting from the tension that has persisted among Michigan Democrats after El-Sayed’s acrimonious primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. Among the Democratic nominee’s detractors are a sitting congresswoman, Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., who has withheld her support for him. Stevens’ likely House successor, state Sen. Jeremy Moss, has also held back on endorsing El-Sayed after entertaining early talks on the topic, as Semafor first reported. Moss isn’t the only Jewish Democrat who remains skeptical of El-Sayed’s harsh criticism of Israel and, as a result, hasn’t backed him. Stevens, in an interview, acknowledged “some shifting dynamics” among Democrats. “Republicans have not held a Senate seat in Michigan for 32 years, and it’s hard to believe that this would really be the year that they’d be able to make a comeback,” she said. “But they’re sure as heck trying.” She also hinted she was focused more on campaigning for House candidates and other Democrats in Michigan than on the Senate race; she’s holding a political event this weekend with House candidate Christina Hines to showcase outreach to Black voters. “I want to see Hakeem Jeffries become the speaker of the House [on the strength of] a place called Michigan,” she said. The View From Voters Attendees at El-Sayed and Ocasio-Cortez’s stop at Northern Michigan University in Marquette contextualized their own excitement around a broader concern that Michigan voters outside the room would view the two as too far left. “Most of my friends would think AOC is too liberal,” said Phil DeGabriele, a 70-year-old retiree from Negaunee. Younger voters were more easily energized by the progressives. Arthur Pichette, a 20-year-old junior at Northern Michigan University, said El-Sayed was “like a breath of fresh air” and that it was “nice” to have El-Sayed and Ocasio-Cortez plainly laying out their views. Nicholas’s view It’s striking to see how boldly El-Sayed and Ocasio-Cortez are already trying to build out a progressive coalition — before he learns whether he needs the fraying parts of the existing Democratic base to beat Rogers. But one thing we’ve known about El-Sayed since the start of his primary race: He’s confident. Talking up a seven-point win isn’t something I see a lot of swing-state candidates do. So if El-Sayed wins, he should be ready for an immediate question about who he plans to wield his new influence for in 2028. It could be his ally Ocasio-Cortez; it could be himself . Notable Bridge Detroit reported on El-Sayed’s potential weakness with Black voters in Detroit. MS NOW covered Rogers’ delicate dance around Trump on the trade war. Ocasio-Cortez’s campaign just transferred $1 million to an effort to elect El-Sayed, The New York Times reported

events.title: Ethiopia sets up Tigray caretaker government as ex-fighters seek return to civilian life
events.summary: Ethiopia's government has set up a six-month caretaker administration for Tigray following renewed fighting in the region NAIROBI, Kenya -- Ethiopia's government set up a six-month caretaker administration for Tigray following renewed fighting in the region, as hundreds of former combatants registered Friday for a program to help them return to civilian life. The new administration is expected to restore public services, help displaced people return and prepare for an election within six months under federal oversight, according to the office of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed . The announcement follows the withdrawal of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front rebel group, or TPLF, from Mekelle and the entry of government-allied fighters into the regional capital on Oct. 4. Renewed fighting in the northern region in recent weeks has effectively shattered a 2022 peace agreement that ended a devastating two-year war. Ethiopia also has accused Eritrean troops of occupying parts of its territory, while Eritrea condemned Ethiopia for what it called a declaration of war. At Mekelle’s Tigray Martyrs’ Memorial Monument, former fighters lined up to register with the authorities, some carrying papers or sheltering under umbrellas. Registration began Wednesday. Authorities declined to say how many former fighters had signed up. “We were called upon by the TPLF to rejoin our former comrades and units, and doing so was even considered mandatory,” said Filmon Gebreselassie, a 33-year-old day laborer. “However, I did not want to return (to war). I decided instead to focus on raising my children.” He said that he had disarmed after the 2022 peace agreement in Tigray, but had been unable to register before the reintegration program was suspended as new tensions rose. Other former fighters were also signing up because they didn't want to fight again, he said. Many young men at the registration office declined interviews, citing fear of retaliation from the TPLF. In an Oct. 14 statement on its official Facebook page, the TPLF denounced Tigrayans collaborating with the federal government as “traitors” and said they would face “accountability and public judgment.” Human Rights Watch reported in June that Tigrayan authorities then in charge of Mekelle had ordered former fighters back to their units in a compulsory recruitment campaign. A TPLF spokesperson said those defending the region were volunteers, according to the watchdog. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs' Hurricane Isaias: At least 4 dead as Isaias downgraded The disarmament, demobilization and reintegration of former Tigrayan fighters is part of the 2022 peace agreement. Abiy’s office accused the TPLF of obstructing the agreement and said that the latest fighting ended in its defeat. The rebels urged their forces to continue fighting and called on Tigrayans to support them. Magnus Taylor, deputy Horn of Africa director at the International Crisis Group, cautioned against equating the loss of towns with an end to fighting. “We shouldn’t imagine that this conflict is completely over just because the TPLF has lost Mekelle,” he told The Associated Press on Wednesday. Capturing towns and roads would hamper Tigrayan fighters without necessarily securing the vast rural areas where the rebel forces regrouped during the previous war, Taylor said. Ethiopia also has accused Eritrean troops of occupying its territory, an allegation that the AP couldn't independently verify. Eritrea described Ethiopia’s assertion that it was taking self-defense measures as a declaration of war. Taylor warned that the proximity of the countries’ forces increased the risk of a wider conflict. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged de-escalation in a call with Abiy on Wednesday, according to the U.S. State Department. Eritrean troops fought alongside Ethiopian forces during the 2020-2022 war, which caused about 500,000 civilian deaths through violence, famine and collapsed health services, according to researchers at Ghent University in Belgium. Amir Aman Kiyaro in Hamburg, Germany, Filmon Equar Hailu in Mekelle, Ethiopia, and Desmond Tiro in Nairobi, Kenya, contributed to this report. events.title: My Dubai Salary: 'I earn up to Dh45,000 a month coaching wellness to women in midlife’
events.summary: Monika Singh arrived in Dubai 12 years ago with a dentistry degree from India and a plan to sit her Dubai Health Authority licensing exams to practise in the UAE. Then she started attending group workout classes while she studied, discovered a love for dance fitness and never looked back. Today, she runs Monika Sphere, a women's wellness coaching business specialising in women in midlife, a niche she arrived at through her own experience with perimenopause after having her son, now seven. She now works exclusively within Arabian Ranches 1 and 2, coaches 23 clients, and earns between Dh42,000 and Dh45,000 a month. What was your first job? Before I started my own thing, I was doing group exercise classes in Fitness First and some other studios across Dubai. That was my starting point in the industry. I was never into fitness , honestly. I started attending dance fitness classes, and it just kind of stayed with me, and I was like, “Oh wow, I really want to do this.” I told my husband; I expressed my feelings to him, and he was very supportive. From there, I started my journey into fitness. I took my Zumba training, then I went into a group exercise leadership programme. Then I did my yoga training, Les Mills Body Balance training, then personal training and sound healing. A lot of things happened, and here I am today. And now? I’ve set up my own company. I have been training 23 ladies, and I'm just around Ranches 1 and 2 – I don't go outside because of commute time, and I also don't have time to go out and train people. My average earnings are Dh42,000 to Dh45,000 a month. My training is not just about typical strength training. Of course, strength training is important for women, but other factors come into play, like mobility, recovery, your sleep, your meditation, and your breathwork. Everything comes together to give you a balanced and sustainable fitness regime. I also specialise in women in midlife. This came to me through my own experience. After I delivered a baby, and as I entered my midlife phase – that is, perimenopause – I realised that my energy was not the same, my sleep was getting affected, and my responsibilities were different. And I realised the same complaint was coming from the women that I coach. Coming from a medical background, I have more understanding of human anatomy and physiology. I decided to dive more into this and study women's wellness, especially in midlife. I took my training, and now I am helping women achieve their goals without punishing themselves. Do you manage to save and invest? Yes, I do save. I'm not investing yet, but I do take care of my daily routine. I have a boy – seven years old – so I manage his school fees, then take care of my car loan, and some house chores. I keep around Dh3,000 to Dh4,000 aside for household expenses, and the rest I save. My husband takes care of the rest of the house. Growing up, were you taught how to handle your finances? When I was in university studying dentistry , we were given a very small amount of pocket money, and you had to manage that throughout the week. You wouldn't get more than that – that was the rule set by our parents, because in India it's like that. That's how I learnt how to manage my expenses. Honestly, I didn't learn anything about investing because we were not given the right to make any decisions on that. It was all my father who used to do that, not us. What are your financial goals? Currently, my goal is to launch my online portal. I have been saving for that because launching an online portal, an app, and everything else is expensive. Long-term, we have a plan to get a new, bigger house after I launch my online portal, once it becomes successful and once we start getting more and more income. That is our first plan. Where do you want to see yourself in the next 10 years? I want to be a known personality, a successful businesswoman – among people in the UAE who are known for their work.

events.title: IEEE Offers More Services to Cities That Want to Be Smarter
events.summary: More and more city governments are using advanced technologies to improve livability for their residents. Municipalities use data from smartphones and sensors for traffic enforcement, traffic control, and waste management. They also have implemented artificial intelligence and deep learning programs. Dubai , Paris , and Coral Gables , Fla., are among the cities that have invested heavily in programs to become smarter. But along with the conveniences that come with a smart city transition, there have been challenges including safety and privacy issues and eroding relationships between residents and city officials. Although many initiatives have delivered real innovations, not all have been successful. Inefficient global coordination has hindered projects with unclear standards, socioeconomic differences, and a lack of worldwide governance, leading to a disconnect between the technologies and the ability to adapt to them. Citizens’ trust in the technologies suffers because of privacy breaches, personal data leaks, and other issues. Finding solutions Smart city projects are complex and expensive endeavors that involve politicians, citizens, technocrats, and engineers. Successful projects require citizens to be fully engaged and to have strong collaborations with the participants, especially engineers, as engineering is the cornerstone . Collaboration with universities, research institutions, and technology experts can bridge knowledge gaps on the behavior of complex socio-technical systems. What’s missing, though, is a global platform where those involved can discuss their experiences. To help solve those and other challenges, the IEEE Smart Cities Technical Community (formerly the IEEE Smart Cities Initiative ) was launched in 2013 by IEEE Future Directions , which incubates emerging technologies and new applications of current ones. The technical community provides city leaders and others with credible, unbiased information and educational content developed by IEEE experts. Since then, IEEE Smart Cities has launched services including its flagship International Smart Cities Conference , a media center with educational and technical resources, and a contest to recognize the best smart project completed by city officials. The platforms bring together practicing engineers, academic researchers, policymakers, and city leaders to collaborate and exchange ideas and experiences about moving toward a smart-city model. Better serving humanity In 2021 the IEEE Power & Energy Society began managing the Smart Cities program, which is supported by the IEEE Communications , Industry Applications , and Intelligent Transportation Systems societies and other IEEE entities. Thanks to volunteers’ dedication and determination, IEEE Smart Cities launched several services. But the initiative’s structure limited the development of long-term projects and the creation of new activities. To address the situation, the IEEE Technical Activities Board (TAB) created the second-generation technical community ad hoc committee , also in 2021. It was a pilot program whereby IEEE Smart Cities formed a board of governors to oversee the community’s operations and leadership, and created a policies and procedures manual. In November 2025 IEEE Smart Cities became a TAB technical community . IEEE Smart Cities now Today more than 7,000 volunteers collaborate on various aspects of the community within at least one of the following technical tracks: Smart grid. Smart water management. Green electronics for smart cities. Smart governance and planning. Hydrogen for smart cities. Smart and sustainable campus. Security for smart cities. Smart lighting for cities. Smart mobility for cities. Artificial intelligence for cities. New webinar series, workshops, conferences, educational resources, and other offerings are being created. Two events were launched recently: the IEEE European Technology and Engineering Management Summit , held in May 2025 in Belgium, with the next one planned for 2027; and the IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference , scheduled for 2 to 6 December in Athens. The Smart Cities Ambassadors program aims to raise the technical community’s visibility outside IEEE by holding roundtables and other events at non-IEEE functions. IEEE Smart Cities volunteers are working on launching journals. In addition, standards are being developed in collaboration with the IEEE Standards Association , societies, and councils. The program is collaborating with the Open and Agile Smart Cities and Communities network, the Instituto de Competitividad e Innovación para el Desarrollo y Transferencia de Tecnología, and the International Project Management Association . All of those actions have the ultimate objective of boosting IEEE Smart Cities’ growth and sustainability, as well as strengthening the leadership and educational offerings to technical community volunteers. If you would like to volunteer, visit the Smart Cities website .

events.title: $2m payday for home battery owners as heatwave catches grid off guard
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Spring heatwave and coal outages deliver $2m payday for home battery owners Topic: Electricity Production and Distribution On Monday evening this week, self-styled home battery boffins were buzzing with excitement on Reddit. Deep in niche threads, they shared screenshots and boasted about how much money they'd made that afternoon on the National Energy Market (NEM). Electricity prices in New South Wales had suddenly skyrocketed around 3:30pm (AEDT), peaking at $23,107 per megawatt hour (MWh), just shy of the market cap. Prices exceeded $5,000/MWh in 11 separate five-minute intervals. "Rolling power spike pricing, have made $100 in an hour selling 30kw/h," one Reddit user commented. A typical household uses between 15 and 20 kilowatt hours of electricity a day. Screenshots from a Reddit sub where people discuss home batteries. ( Supplied ) A spring heat wave was sweeping the state, pushing temperatures into the mid-30s. At Observatory Hill in Sydney, the mercury spiked at 34.7 degrees, more than 12 degrees above the long-term monthly average. For people with solar panels on their roofs and batteries in their garage, it was a chance to make money selling power back to the grid at much higher rates. "Hot day shenanigans," another Reddit user posted under another earnings screenshot. Tristan Edis is the CEO of Green Energy Markets, an industry analysis company. ( Supplied: Green Energy Markets ) Green Energy Markets CEO Tristan Edis said the price spike was a reminder of an underlying NEM vulnerability in a rapidly warming climate as it tried to manage aging coal plants while building generation and storage. "It's normal for electricity prices to be high when temperatures go noticeably above 30 degrees," Edis said. "What's problematic is that doesn't normally happen in October." Fuelling the extraordinary spike in prices was a confluence of factors. As temperatures climbed, four of NSW's 12 coal-fired generating units were out of action and two were at reduced capacity. The Eraring Power Station is scheduled to shut down in 2029. ( AAP/Greenpeace ) To make matters worse, several high transmission lines were also running below capacity due to maintenance, meaning huge amounts of mostly renewable energy and storage capacity could not be delivered to Sydney just when it needed it most. Australian energy intelligence firm GridScout said the energy was instead curtailed, or throttled at the source, because the high-voltage network could not transport more electricity. "Technical curtailment peaked at (2,800 megawatts), with renewables and batteries in Southern NSW being the most heavily affected," the firm noted on social media. "This was all while prices were above $10,000/MWh." So hot temperatures drove up demand just when less electricity was available. Amid the chaos, market watchers were also stunned by an unusual phenomenon. Just after 3pm AEDT, as demand soared, NSW prices on the spot electricity market started whipsawing dramatically. They jumped from about $200/MWh to more than $1,300/MWh, fell to $766, hit the $23,000 market ceiling minutes later, then plunged again. Dave Smith, a wholesale power market designer, said the wild price gyrations appeared to have been driven by a new force in energy — Australia's growing fleet of household batteries. In the national grid, the Australian Energy Market Operator sets prices every five minutes. It does so choosing the lowest-priced "bids" of whichever generators are offering to meet supply. The price paid is the cost of the highest-priced bid required to meet demand in that five-minute period. According to Smith, the squeeze in NSW on Monday drew a predictable response from the market. Prices rose sharply as supplies struggled to keep pace with demand. Tesla releases plans for Australia's largest EV charging hub More problems emerging along WA's high-profile 'electric highway' Pacific's undersea treasure is worth billions, but some say we'll never see it The key features Australian homes may have in the future Among those responding were the legions of household battery owners, who were getting alerts on their phones telling them to sell their surplus power to tap into soaring prices. But unlike most energy providers, these batteries sit "behind the meter", meaning the market operator cannot see nor control them. When prices spiked on Monday, households with batteries sold big amounts of power into the system, only to pull back when prices fell in the next five-minute interval. At all times, Smith said, AEMO was on the back foot and playing catch-up.

events.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
events.summary: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal. At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around. Still, the Indian cases appear to be worse in one respect, which is what the agents saw: In Australia, OpenAI said it found no evidence its agents touched individuals’ medical or criminal records, even after they wrote files inside a Medicare statistics system, while in India, agents read personal data and confidential business records. And unlike earlier incidents, each disclosed by a single lab, India’s case involved agents from multiple providers. CERT-In did not name the providers or affected organizations, or say whether the agents altered any systems. TechCrunch has reached out to CERT-In for more information. For now, the closest parallel seems to be Anthropic’s July disclosure of Claude breaking into three companies’ systems during testing using basic techniques like weak passwords. In India, as in Anthropic’s cases, the affected organizations had not detected the intrusions on their own. The disclosures have left governments relying on AI companies causing these breaches to voluntarily disclose rogue AI agent activity. events.title: Palisades nuclear reactor restart continues despite work environment safety findings
events.summary: The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission has granted permission to Holtec International, owner of the Palisades nuclear reactor , to retrieve a potentially compromised fuel assembly, although the plant received a warning about its work environment. At some point after August 30, as new fuel was being lowered into the reactor, one of the fuel assemblies tipped, causing the plant's planned restart to be placed on hold. If Holtec successfully retrieves the fuel assembly, efforts to restart the plant are likely to move forward with NRC oversight. The Palisades reactor, bought by Holtec after it was decommissioned in 2022, has become a poster child for the US nuclear energy renaissance driven by artificial intelligence data centres. The NRC said no radiation was released during the incident at the reactor, in Covert , Michigan. Amid the controversy, the NRC sent a letter to Holtec following an inspection that determined that although Palisades maintained a safety-conscious work environment overall, “a chilled work environment” existed in the supply chain and quality assurance departments. The NRC explained: “Employees in these two work departments are hesitant to raise safety concerns using all available avenues without fear of retaliation.” Patrick O’Brien, Holtec director of government affairs and communications, said the company was “taking actions to address these issues and will continue our work to maintain and strengthen a healthy safety-conscious work environment”. But the response to the NRC findings has failed to calm fears among those concerned about the plant's work environment and the restarting of “ zombie reactors ”. “Holtec's unprecedented restart of the Palisades zombie reactor will risk a Chernobyl or Fukushima-scale catastrophe a hundred yards from the shoreline of the Great Lakes, drinking water supply for more than 40 million people in eight US states, two Canadian provinces and a large number of Indigenous Nations,” said Kevin Kamps, executive director for environmental advocacy group Don't Waste Michigan. Arnie Gundersen, a nuclear engineer and expert adviser for the organisation, called the NRC's decision to approve Holtec's strategy for retrieving the tipped fuel assembly “ironic”. “In the last four weeks, Palisades lost control and tipped a nuclear fuel bundle and couldn’t get it out, nine out of 15 licensed reactor operators failed their exam, and more than half of the people in their quality assurance and procurement departments feel they will be fired by management if they bring concerns forward,” he said, and yet “ironically … the NRC just gave them permission to begin loading fuel again!” 📍 NRC senior managers recently visited Palisades nuclear plant as part of our continued oversight to ensure the historic restart is done safely. pic.twitter.com/9SLRdJejyT — NRC (@NRCgov) October 9, 2026 He added that the subsequent report from the NRC indicated that the “fuel assembly exhibits significant bowing”. In a statement to The National , a spokesperson for the NRC reiterated that the findings related to a chilled work environment were limited to the Palisades “supply chain and quality assurance departments”, adding that the government agency “did not identify any violations or significant plant safety issues but has concerns about the work environment's impact on these departments.” That spokesperson also said that the NRC will “continue to verify that safety requirements are met”. As for approving Holtec’s method of retrieving the tipped fuel assembly, the NRC indicated that its “specialists and resident inspectors will continue monitoring removal activities.” In a statement, however, Holtec said that it appreciated the government agency's decision. “The proposed recovery approach was supported by engineering evaluations addressing structural integrity, fuel handling, thermal conditions, and radiation protection,” Holtec said. A source close to Holtec recently told The National that the company hoped to have Palisades back online by March 2027. Holtec has yet to provide a timeline. 📍 As Palisades begins loading fuel into the reactor, our inspectors have been on site ensuring this activity meets safety and security requirements. This historic step moves the plant closer to restart — an extraordinary milestone for nuclear energy and the NRC. pic.twitter.com/qGfoCfwaYD — NRC (@NRCgov) September 2, 2026 “Palisades will return to service when all required work is complete and all federal requirements and industry standards are met,” Mr O'Brien said. “Our team of more than 1,000 nuclear professionals continues this work in parallel with the fuel assembly recovery effort.” Before shutting down 2022, the Palisades reactor was no stranger to controversy. In 2012, an NRC report warned about the work culture at the plant, where it said safety concerns were often dismissed. In 2016, security staff were placed on leave from the plant, which was then owned by Entergy, for failing to properly follow fire prevention protocol. In October 2025, a worker at Palisades fell off a refuelling bridge into a pool of water, but was not seriously injured.

events.title: Ecommerce confronts AI shopping agents ahead of holiday season
events.summary: This coming holiday season, brands will have a new type of shopper to court: AI agents. Cheq, a cybersecurity company that verifies AI shopping agents, says it recorded a 100x surge in agentic traffic over a 45-day period following the release of consumer AI agents like Instinct and Meta’s Muse. While agents still make up a small fraction of online shoppers, they’re growing quickly, especially among a constant drumbeat of consumer agent releases, Cheq CEO Guy Tytunovich said. But not everyone is on board: Amazon and eBay have blocked agents to reinforce control over their ads businesses and checkout experiences. Consumers are hesitant, too. Shoppers are now as likely to be swayed by an agent’s recommendation as by an influencer, Morning Consult finds, but few are comfortable letting AI make purchases on their behalf. This holiday season will be the first true test of which brands are best at displaying their wares in ways that agents find irresistible. — Jake Angelo

events.title: Why the AI bubble fears are overblown
events.summary: Reed’s view Fear is rising that the AI bubble is about to burst under the weight of mounting debt, as my colleague Liz Hoffman detailed yesterday, including this great quote from an unnamed data-center financier: “We’re not an ATM for your dystopian future.” Perhaps lenders have grown tired of funding the data center buildout, but money is not going to be the thing that finally causes the AI train to go off the rails. Everything is bottlenecked. It’s not just chips, memory, and EUV machines. It’s refrigeration units that cool the GPUs and the raw materials needed to make components, like glass. If it weren’t for this bottlenecked supply chain, it’s likely AI revenues and user numbers would be growing much faster. Every time companies reach a new level of token efficiency, some new use case for AI is born that burns through ever more compute, proving Jevons Paradox . My favorite example of late: Decompiling video games to create mashups , something that used to take people years to do manually can now be done by AI in a weekend. It may be the thing that finally turns Gen-Zers into fans of AI. The total addressable market of AI is roughly 100% of the earth’s population, and demand for it will continue to soar. The enterprise market has only dipped its toes into AI, and the consumer hasn’t even begun to dive in. Anthropic told investors this week that it’s making 85% gross margins. Even if that number is a gross exaggeration, this is a cash cow business. They’ll service their debt obligations, in other words. I agree with the lender who lamented being an ATM for the AI industry, but probably for a different reason. Why would you want to lend money for measly interest payments when you could invest and get a massive return? There’s a reason hyperscalers and neoclouds reached for debt: It’s relatively cheap. Notable Data center firms say that talent and power are two of the main bottlenecks challenging the AI buildout today, Bloomberg reported.

events.title: The Guardian view on the banks: too big to fail cannot mean too big to tax | Editorial
events.summary: Financiers owe their windfalls and bonuses to higher interest rates. Britain should reclaim more for the public and resist City lobbying John Healey is planning to tax British banks, the Guardian revealed , in the forthcoming budget. It’s about time for the chancellor to act. Banks have been raking it in. The campaign group Positive Money reported this summer that Britain’s four biggest banks made £29bn in the first half of this year, up a fifth on 2025. These windfalls owe more to higher interest rates than better products or services. Households and businesses pay more to borrow. Meanwhile, the Bank of England pays the banks tens of billions in interest on their reserves, with the  Treasury footing the bill. The chancellor is said to favour restoring the bank surcharge from 3% to 8%, which could raise around £2bn a year . This would recover a very modest share of the sector’s bonanza. Louis XIV’s finance minister, Jean-Baptiste Colbert, said that “the art of taxation consists in so plucking the goose as to obtain the largest possible amount of feathers with the smallest possible amount of hissing”. Britain’s banks have plenty of feathers. That hasn’t stopped them hissing . The banks say that they already face higher taxes than other companies, that they won’t be able to lend as much, and that their profits won’t last.
